name: The Company takes Bida and Ilorin

summary.text: In early 1897 the Royal Niger Company’s army under George Goldie marched on the two southern emirates of the Caliphate. Bida fell after two days of fighting in late January and its Etsu was deposed; in February Ilorin was shelled and taken. Bida’s own subjects helped the Company: the north-east Yoruba, the Kyadya boatmen and the Yissazhi faction of the old Nupe dynasty, who were given the emirate of Pategi.

moments.title: The march to Ogidi and the Kabba declaration
moments.text: A Company force of 30 European officers and 513 African soldiers leaves Lokoja for Ogidi via Kabba to strike Bida’s army there. The camp has gone, so the Company declares the north-east Yoruba free of Bida. Kabba gives porters and guides for the march to the Niger.

moments.title: The Kyadya change sides
moments.text: Kyadya boatmen under Marike, promised the title of Kuta, ferry the Company across at Kpatagbon and refuse to carry Bida’s retreating army.

moments.title: Bida falls
moments.text: After two days of fighting the town is taken and Etsu Abubakar is deposed.
